title: Weekly Scientific Lineage · 2026-W48
executive_summary:
High-energy transient research this week reveals a tightly coupled physical continuum extending from compact object engines through structured outflows and circumstellar medium (CSM) shocks to multi-wavelength propagation diagnostics. 
- **Engine-Driven Transients & Nuclear Orbits**: The authors of arXiv:2611.28443 demonstrated that AT 2024qfm achieved an unprecedented early peak X-ray luminosity of $L_{\rm x} \approx 10^{44}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ with $L_{\rm x}/L_{\rm opt} \approx 8.4$ at $\delta t \approx 14\,{\rm days}$, demanding an equatorial slow-outflow covering fraction $\phi_0 \lesssim 0.1$ and Thomson optical depth $\tau_{\rm T} < 1$. In galactic nuclei, the authors of arXiv:2611.28220 established that TDE accretion disk drag combined with gravitational wave radiation boosts the survival fraction of Hills-captured stars forming sub-day QPE/rpTDE orbits up to $\sim 30\%$ around $10^6\,M_\odot$ black holes.
- **Fast Radio Bursts & Circum-Burst Media**: The authors of arXiv:2611.26696 revealed that shock propagation through neutral binary wind bubbles after accretion-induced collapse generates a sign reversal in local dispersion measure drift rate $d{\rm DM}_{\rm loc}/dt$ from negative to $+3\text{--}5\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ at $t \approx 9\text{--}22\,{\rm yr}$. Across broad radio bandwidths, the authors of arXiv:2611.28250 and arXiv:2611.28251 used joint CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 detections to confirm non-repeating FRB emission over $>1\,{\rm GHz}$ bandwidth with median $\beta = -0.3 \pm 0.4$, while identifying scatter-induced phase mixing that flattens low-frequency polarization angle swings; concurrently, the authors of arXiv:2611.28334 derived an unevolved local volumetric rate density $\Phi_0 = 1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3} \times 10^5\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ and median host dispersion measure $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host, med}^\prime = 199^{+34}_{-36}\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}}$.
- **Super-Eddington Accretion & Relativistic Outflows**: The authors of arXiv:2611.30018 modeled two-fluid radiation-hydrodynamical ULXP columns, establishing that radiation sonic surfaces rigidly cluster at $r_{\rm sonic} \simeq 15.0\,{\rm km}$ while thermal mound heights scale between $0.07\,{\rm km}$ and $1.53\,{\rm km}$; observationally, the authors of arXiv:2611.27693 detected a relativistically blueshifted ultrafast outflow with $v_{\rm LOS} \approx -0.1c$ in RX J0209.6-7427, and the authors of arXiv:2611.26733 uncovered an extreme transient ULX in NGC 1300 with dynamic range $R > 715$.
- **MHD Jet Physics & Relativistic Blastwaves**: The authors of arXiv:2611.28376 simulated multi-Mpc jets, demonstrating that high injection Lorentz factors $\Gamma = 12$ suppress transverse MHD instabilities to allow propagation across $\sim 9\,{\rm Mpc}$ in void environments, while the authors of arXiv:2611.28237 identified the Dual Horizon-MAD state in binary black holes with horizon flux saturation $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 20$ launching Poynting jets at $1\%$ efficiency.
- **Supernova Remnants & Dense Nuclear Physics**: The authors of arXiv:2611.29910 resolved 3D Doppler velocity splitting in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve, measuring a front-to-rear velocity asymmetry of $\sim 16\%$ ($v_{\rm front} = -3320\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ vs $v_{\rm back} = +3920\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while the authors of arXiv:2611.27628 and arXiv:2611.27669 resolved how Landau quantization suppresses crustal Urca cooling to sustain anomalously hot magnetars and how nuclear uncertainties cancel against Love number variations in neutron star tidal deformability.

overview_matrix.domain: Relativistic Jets & Binary Black Hole Electrodynamics
overview_matrix.key_question: How do relativistic jets survive destructive MHD instabilities across megaparsec scales, and how do binary black hole accretion flows channel horizon magnetic flux?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2611.28376] (The authors): 3D RMHD simulations show that relativistic jets with initial bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma = 12$ injected into underdense void media accelerate to $\Gamma > 20$ via recollimation shocks, suppressing Kelvin-Helmholtz and kink modes (power $\sum |F(k)|^2/N \le 10^{-2}$) to reach $\sim 9\,{\rm Mpc}$ in $19.6\,{\rm Myr}$.\n- [arXiv:2611.28237] (The authors): 3D full GRMHD simulations of equal-mass binary black holes establish a Dual Horizon-MAD state where horizon magnetic flux saturates at $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 20$, driving intermittent minidisks and Poynting jets with efficiency $\eta = 1\%$ and characteristic orbital frequency modulations ($f \sim 0.9f_{\rm orb}, 1.8f_{\rm orb}$).\n- [arXiv:2611.26682] (The authors): Synthetic polarimetric modeling demonstrates that soft X-ray polarimetry ($0.2\text{--}0.4\,{\rm keV}$) breaks leptonic/hadronic degeneracies in HSP blazars with predicted polarization degree ${\rm PD} \approx 6.6\%\text{--}8.4\%$, whereas leptonic models yield zero MeV polarization.
overview_matrix.significance: Demonstrates that relativistic thrust in underdense cosmic voids is the decisive mechanism preventing MHD instability disruption in giant radio jets, while binary black hole mergers under magnetically arrested accretion exhibit synchronized dual-horizon jet launching.

overview_matrix.key_question: How do crustal Landau quantization and high-density equation-of-state uncertainties govern magnetar thermal balance and neutron star macroscopic observables?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2611.27628] (The authors): Quantizing magnetic fields in magnetar crusts induce de Haas-van Alphen oscillations in electron Fermi energy, freezing electrons into the lowest Landau level at $B \gtrsim 2\times 10^{16}\,{\rm G}$ to quench Urca neutrino cooling and maintain anomalous surface temperatures of $k_{\rm B}T \sim 0.28\text{--}0.72\,{\rm keV}$.\n- [arXiv:2611.27669] (The authors): Variance decomposition of $1.4\,M_\odot$ neutron star parameters proves that an extreme anti-correlation ($\rho = -0.952$) between logarithmic radius $\ln R$ and Love number $\ln k_2$ cancels nuclear experimental constraints on tidal deformability down to $1.38\%$, which can be broken by pairing $\sigma_R = 0.3\,{\rm km}$ radius measurements with $\sigma_{\ln \widetilde{\Lambda}} = 0.1$ binary tides.
overview_matrix.significance: Uncovers the quantum thermodynamic origin of anomalously hot magnetar surfaces via magnetic field-induced Urca quenching, and reveals mathematical degeneracies in core EOS sound speeds that require joint tidal-radius measurements to break.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Magnetar Circumstellar Dynamics and Multi-Station FRB Demographics
thematic_highlights.summary: This week marks a major synthesis in understanding fast radio bursts as environmental probes. Dynamical models of accretion-induced collapse demonstrate that the multi-year secular drift and sign reversal of local dispersion measure ($d{\rm DM}_{\rm loc}/dt \sim +3\text{--}5\,{\rm pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$) naturally arise when asymmetric ejecta shock-ionize neutral circumstellar wind shells. Simultaneously, coordinated CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 dual-station observations confirm that non-repeating FRBs emit across $>1\,{\rm GHz}$ of instantaneous bandwidth with median spectral index $\beta = -0.3 \pm 0.4$ and spectral turnovers at $\sim 720\,{\rm MHz}$, while polarimetric modeling demonstrates that low-frequency multipath scattering systematically depolarizes bursts and suppresses intrinsic polarization angle swings. Cosmological population synthesis from Catalog 2 tightly anchors the local volumetric rate to $\Phi_0 = 1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3} \times 10^5\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ while revealing minimal cosmic rate evolution ($n = 0.5 \pm 0.4$).

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Unveiling Central Engines in Optical Transients, TDEs, and Blastwaves
thematic_highlights.summary: Observations and hydrodynamical models this week challenge canonical isotropic assumptions in explosive transients. In the luminous fast blue optical transient AT 2024qfm, an extreme peak X-ray luminosity of $L_{\rm x} \approx 10^{44}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ and late-time radio outflow entering dense CSM indicate an asymmetric geometry where a low optical depth ($\ extrm{Thomson}\ \tau_{\rm T} < 1$) along the line of sight prevents high-energy reprocessing into the optical band. In galactic nuclei, Hills-captured stars undergoing repeated collisions with viscously spreading TDE disks experience hydrodynamic drag that counteracts two-body relaxation, boosting the survival rate of sub-day repeating nuclear transients (QPEs) up to $\sim 30\%$. Furthermore, high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with XRISM/Resolve resolves the Doppler line splitting of Tycho's SNR into separate front and rear shells, discovering a $\sim 16\%$ expansion velocity asymmetry ($v_{\rm front} = -3320\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ vs $v_{\rm back} = +3920\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) with chemical segregation between Fe and Si.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Physics of Super-Critical Accretion and Relativistic Outflows
thematic_highlights.summary: Theoretical and observational breakthroughs elucidate the boundary layer dynamics and wind launching mechanisms in super-Eddington systems. Self-consistent two-fluid radiation-hydrodynamical modeling of ultraluminous X-ray pulsars demonstrates that the radiation sonic surface rigidly pins at $r_{\rm sonic} \simeq 15.0\,{\rm km}$ across varying magnetic fields and accretion rates, while thermal mound heights adjust dynamically to enforce surface stagnation. Complementing this theory, high-resolution spectroscopy of RX J0209.6-7427 directly detects a relativistically blueshifted ultrafast outflow with $v_{\rm LOS} \approx -0.1c$, confirming that radiation pressure drives massive outflows in magnetized neutron stars. In the extragalactic population, the discovery of transient ULX X32 in NGC 1300 with an extreme dynamic range $R > 715$ demonstrates dramatic structural transitions between sub-Eddington and super-critical accretion states.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Relativistic Jet Dynamics, MAD Accretion, and Blazar Electrodynamics
thematic_highlights.summary: Large-scale 3D relativistic simulations and polarimetric projections clarify the survival of cosmic jets and horizon-scale magnetic flux. 3D RMHD simulations of mega-scale jets reveal that an initial bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma = 12$ injected into underdense void environments accelerates via recollimation shocks to $\Gamma > 20$, effectively stabilizing the jet backbone against Kelvin-Helmholtz and current-driven kink modes to sustain propagation over $\sim 9\,{\rm Mpc}$. On black hole horizon scales, full GRMHD simulations of equal-mass binaries discover the Dual Horizon-MAD state, characterized by dimensionless flux saturation at $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 20$ and periodic jet launching at $1\%$ efficiency. In blazars, soft X-ray polarimetric modeling between $0.2\text{--}0.4\,{\rm keV}$ proves decisive in distinguishing leptonic from hadronic synchrotron mechanisms.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Crustal Quantum Microphysics and Dense Core Equation of State
thematic_highlights.summary: Microphysical calculations of neutron star interiors provide direct insights into observed macroscopic thermal and mechanical properties. In magnetar crusts, magnetic field quantization induces de Haas-van Alphen oscillations that modulate electron capture thresholds; at extreme fields ($B \gtrsim 2\times 10^{16}\,{\rm G}$), electrons freeze into the lowest Landau level, quenching crustal Urca neutrino cooling and naturally explaining the persistent anomalous surface heat ($k_{\rm B}T \sim 0.28\text{--}0.72\,{\rm keV}$). On core scales, variance decomposition of TOV equilibrium equations demonstrates that strong anti-correlations between stellar radius and tidal Love number ($k_2$) suppress nuclear precision propagation, proving that breaking EOS degeneracies requires simultaneous constraints from gravitational-wave tidal deformability and NICER pulse-profile modeling.

papers.title: From Binary Wind to Radio Burst: Dispersion-Measure Evolution after Accretion-induced Collapse
papers.result: Along polar directions ($\theta \le \theta_{\rm cav} = 20^\circ$, covering $\sim 6\%$ of the solid angle), ejecta encounter the evacuated cavity wall directly at $t_{\rm hit} \simeq 1.9\ \mathrm{yr}$ with ${\rm DM}_{\rm sh,ejc} = 0$ for $t \le t_{\rm hit}$. Along non-polar sightlines ($\sim 94\%$), forward shocks cross the wind termination shock at $t_{\rm ts} \simeq 2.9\text{--}6.1\ \mathrm{yr}$, the shocked-wind contact discontinuity at $t_{\rm cw} \simeq 12\text{--}23\ \mathrm{yr}$, and the outer wind-bubble shock at $t_{\rm wb} \simeq 31\text{--}113\ \mathrm{yr}$. While unshocked ejecta dilute as ${\rm DM}_{\rm ejc} \propto t^{-2}$, shock ionization of upstream neutral circumstellar shells produces a sign reversal in $d{\rm DM}_{\rm loc}/dt$ from negative to positive at $t \simeq 9\text{--}22\ \mathrm{yr}$, reaching $+3\text{--}5\ \mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ in dense ambient clouds ($n_{\rm ext} = 500\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$). In contrast, fully pre-ionized upstream media produce monotonic declines (${\rm DM}_{\rm sh,ejc} \propto t^{-7/8}$ for wind profile $s=2$).
papers.problem: What physical mechanisms drive the secular multi-year evolution and sign reversals of local dispersion measure (${\rm DM}_{\rm loc}$) observed in repeating fast radio bursts, particularly those situated in old stellar environments where long-delay formation pathways like accretion-induced collapse (AIC) operate within complex, pre-shaped circumstellar wind bubbles?
papers.method: The authors develop an angle-dependent hydrodynamic model coupling aspherical homologous AIC ejecta ($M_{\rm ejc}, E_K$, prolate aspect ratio $\mathcal{A} = v_{\rm pol}/v_{\rm eq} = 1.5$, density power-law $\rho_{\rm ejc} \propto t^{n-3}r^{-n}$ with $n=10, \delta=0$) with a multi-zoned binary wind bubble ($t_w = 5000\ \mathrm{yr}$, $v_w = 1000\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, polar cavity $\theta_{\rm cav} = 20^\circ$). Following shock breakout into non-self-similar strata, the flow in each angular sector is integrated using a one-zone thin-shell momentum equation: $(\mu_{\rm ejc}+\mu_{\rm pre})\frac{dV_{\rm cd}}{dt}=\dot{\mu}_{\rm ejc}(u_{\rm ejc}-V_{\rm cd})+\dot{\mu}_{\rm pre}(u_{\rm pre}-V_{\rm cd})+P R_{\rm cd}^{2}$, accounting for adiabatic expansion $P\,dV$ and ionization transitions.
papers.reason: Accretion-induced collapse (AIC) of massive white dwarfs in sculpted binary wind environments provides an attractive delayed formation channel for repeating FRBs in old stellar populations. The paper constructs an angle-dependent hydrodynamic toy model that naturally accounts for secular DM evolution, slope breaks, and sign reversals without relying on burst-associated photoionization.

papers.title: Blazars through the eyes of REDSoX and GOSoX
papers.result: For HSP blazars, soft X-ray polarimetry at $0.2-0.4\ \mathrm{keV}$ provides robust discrimination with predicted $\mathrm{PD} \approx 6.57\% - 8.38\%$ (e.g. Mrk 421 with $F_{0.2-0.4\,\mathrm{keV}} \approx 1.94 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ well above $\mathrm{MDP} = 1.19\%$), whereas leptonic models predict $\mathrm{PD} \approx 0\%$ in the MeV range ($0.2-5\ \mathrm{MeV}$, COSI) compared to $\approx 11\%$ in GOSoX. For LSP templates (BL Lac), $F_{0.2-0.4\,\mathrm{keV}} = 8.70_{-6.61}^{+6.61} \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ yields $\mathrm{PD} = 7.18_{-0.67}^{+0.49}\%$ with $\mathrm{MDP} = 3.09\%$ and an $89.2\%$ duty cycle.
papers.problem: The high-energy emission mechanism in blazars is degenerate between leptonic models (SSC/EC with lower polarization) and hadronic models (proton synchrotron and cascades with higher polarization), while polarimetric observations below $1\ \mathrm{keV}$ remain completely unexplored.
papers.method: Multi-wavelength SEDs are modeled with Bjet-MCMC and JetSeT for blazar templates (BL Lac, BZB J0211+1051, Mrk 501) across leptonic, hadronic, and hybrid models. For REDSoX/GOSoX ($0.2-0.4\ \mathrm{keV}$), source count rate is evaluated via $R_{\rm S} = \sum A_{\rm eff}(E)\,n_E(E)\,\Delta E$, and the 99% confidence minimum detectable polarization is calculated as ${\rm MDP}_{99}[\%] = \frac{4.291}{\mu\sqrt{R_{\rm S}T}} \times 100$ assuming $\mu = 0.95$ with exposure times $T = 300\ \mathrm{ks}$ (HSP) and $T = 1\ \mathrm{Ms}$ (LSP/ISP).
papers.reason: The paper investigates the observational feasibility of future soft X-ray polarimeters (REDSoX and GOSoX) to break degeneracies between leptonic and hadronic emission models in relativistic blazar jets.

papers.title: Effects of Preionisation in Radiative Shocks IV. A Spectral Grid Library of fully Radiative Shock Models with Time--Dependent Precursor
papers.result: Precursor line ratios are governed by shock velocity via $\Psi = Q/v_{\mathrm{s}} \propto v_{\mathrm{s}}^{\alpha}$ (where $\alpha \gg 2$ at $v_{\mathrm{s}} \sim 50\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ and $\alpha \to 2$ at high velocity). As gas density increases, ram pressure $P_{\rm ram} = \rho v^2$ dominates over magnetic pressure $P_B = B^2 / (8\pi)$. For $v_{\rm shock} > 400\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $[\mathrm{O\ I}]/\mathrm{H}\alpha$ line ratios remain flat and are up to $0.4\ \mathrm{dex}$ higher than MAPPINGS III.
papers.problem: Investigates the self-consistent multi-zone structure and EUV bidirectional radiative transfer of radiative shocks and their time-dependent precursors when downstream ionization fronts travel slower than the shock front.
papers.method: Solves 1D plane-parallel Rankine-Hugoniot flow equations with gas pressure $P_{\rm gas} = n k T = \frac{\rho k T}{\mu m}$, ram pressure $P_{\rm ram} = \rho v^2$, and magnetic pressure $P_B = B^2 / (8\pi)$, incorporating non-equilibrium time-dependent photoionization and the CHIANTI 10 atomic database across $v_{\rm s} = 100 - 1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $n_{\rm H} = 0.01 - 100\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, and $B = 10^{-4} - 100\ \mu\mathrm{G}$.
papers.reason: The library delivers an updated radiative shock grid with time-dependent precursors, providing quantitative emission line diagnostics for shock-driven circumstellar medium interactions and supernova remnants.

papers.title: NGC 1300: A rich reservoir of ultraluminous X-ray sources
papers.result: Identified 42 X-ray sources within the $D_{25}$ optical extent of NGC 1300 ($d = 20.7\ \mathrm{Mpc}$), establishing a census of 6 confirmed off-nuclear ULXs ($L_{\rm X} \ge 10^{39}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$: X2, X11, X18, X21, X29, X32) and 13 ULX candidates. Discovered a new transient ULX, X32, exhibiting an extreme luminosity ratio $R = L_{\rm X,max}/L_{\rm X,UL} > 715$ with peak luminosity $L_{\rm X,max} \simeq 1.46 \times 10^{40}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$ ($L_{\rm X}^{\rm unabs} \simeq 1.30 \times 10^{40}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$) and a broadened-disk multi-color accretion spectrum ($k T_{\rm in} = 1.37_{-0.16}^{+0.21}\ \mathrm{keV}$). Across 12 epochs, the cumulative X-ray luminosity function (XLF) power-law slope spans $\beta \simeq 0.66\text{--}1.00$ ($N(>L_{\rm X}) \propto L_{\rm X}^{-\beta}$).
papers.problem: How the host galaxy environment and suppressed bar star formation govern the spatial distribution, spectral transitions, and long-term variability of high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) and ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs, $L_{\rm X} \ge 10^{39}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$), and whether transient ULXs represent super-Eddington accretion regimes onto neutron stars or stellar-mass black holes.
papers.method: Analyzed 12 archival and newly acquired Chandra/ACIS-S epochs spanning >15 years (2009–2025) complemented by Swift/XRT monitoring. Performed point-source detection using CIAO `wavdetect` in the $0.3\text{--}10\ \mathrm{keV}$ band and computed unabsorbed luminosities via $L_{\rm X} = 4\pi d^2 F_{\rm X}$ ($d = 20.7\ \mathrm{Mpc}$) assuming an absorbed power law with $\Gamma = 1.7$ and Galactic $N_{\rm H} = 2 \times 10^{20}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$. Evaluated spectral hardness ratio $\mathrm{HR} = (H - S)/(H + S)$ ($S: 0.3\text{--}2\ \mathrm{keV}$, $H: 2\text{--}10\ \mathrm{keV}$) and soft/hard colors $(M - S)/(S + M + H)$ and $(H - M)/(S + M + H)$ ($S: 0.3\text{--}1.0\ \mathrm{keV}$, $M: 1.0\text{--}2.0\ \mathrm{keV}$, $H: 2.0\text{--}8.0\ \mathrm{keV}$). Carried out periodicity searches via the $Z_n^2$ test for sources with $>100$ photons, evaluated variability significance $S_{\rm var} = (L_{\rm X,max} - L_{\rm X,min})/\sqrt{\sigma_{\rm max}^2 + \sigma_{\rm min}^2}$, and fitted cumulative XLFs via maximum likelihood.
papers.reason: This study provides multi-epoch Chandra and Swift observational constraints on the ULX and HMXB population, spectral states, and extreme transient behavior in NGC 1300, directly relevant to compact object high-energy observations and super-Eddington accretion physics.

papers.title: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
papers.result: NuSTAR broadband spectroscopy reveals a maximum post-shock plasma temperature $kT_{\rm max} = 44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}\,\mathrm{keV}$, neutral Fe K$\alpha$ emission ($E = 6.47^{+0.10}_{-0.07}\,\mathrm{keV}$, equivalent width $161^{+68}_{-65}\,\mathrm{eV}$), and a Compton reflection component with amplitude $R = 0.37^{+0.15}_{-0.13}$, constraining the white dwarf mass to $M_{\rm WD} \ge 0.85\,M_\odot$. Time-resolved spectroscopy indicates that while the mass accretion rate modulates by a factor of $\sim 4.5$ with normalization $\mathrm{Norm} \sim (1.46\text{--}6.26) \times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the post-shock temperature remains remarkably stable at $kT_{\rm max} \approx 44\text{--}47\,\mathrm{keV}$.
papers.problem: Constraining the post-shock accretion column temperature, white dwarf mass $M_{\rm WD}$, shock height $H$, Compton reflection properties, and investigating the mechanism underlying shock temperature stability during accretion rate variations in the asynchronous polar IGR J19552+0044.
papers.method: Simultaneous spectral modeling of NuSTAR FPMA and FPMB data over 3–79 keV using $\texttt{const}*\texttt{TBabs}*(\texttt{gaussian}+\texttt{reflect}*\texttt{mkcflow})$, combined with 3–40 keV timing and hardness ratio analysis across a 107 ks observation.
papers.reason: This study presents the first hard X-ray spectroscopy of the short-period asynchronous polar IGR J19552+0044, providing key constraints on accretion shock physics and white dwarf parameters relevant to compact object high-energy observations.

papers.title: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
papers.result: Low-lying thermal nuclear excitations enhance crustal Urca neutrino luminosity by $\sim 1.2$ orders of magnitude over ground-state transitions. At weak fields ($B \lesssim 10^{14.5}\,\mathrm{G}$), $L_\nu$ matches the zero-field case, whereas strong fields trigger de Haas-van Alphen oscillations in electron chemical potential $\mu_e$, producing non-monotonic oscillations across the Urca window $|Q_{\rm EC}| - k_B T \lesssim \mu_e \lesssim |Q_{\rm EC}| + k_B T$; at $B \gtrsim 2 \times 10^{16}\,\mathrm{G}$, electrons freeze into the lowest Landau level, suppressing and quenching crustal Urca cooling to sustain higher surface temperatures ($k_B T \sim 0.28\text{--}0.72\,\mathrm{keV}$).
papers.problem: The persistent observational problem of anomalously high surface temperatures ($k_B T \sim 0.28\text{--}0.72\,\mathrm{keV}$) in magnetars relative to canonical neutron stars ($k_B T \sim 0.01\text{--}0.15\,\mathrm{keV}$), and how quantizing magnetic fields ($B \gg B_c \approx 4.414\times 10^{13}\,\mathrm{G}$) and thermal excitations regulate crustal Urca cooling rates.
papers.method: A continuous radial depth-integration framework for crustal nuclear Urca neutrino luminosity using single-volume loss rate $\mathcal{Q}^{\pm} = \tilde{L}^{\pm}(B) n^{\pm}$ and Fermi energy gradient $a_0 \equiv dW_F/dr = \frac{1}{10}\left(\frac{E_0}{m_e c^2}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\rho_9 Y_e}\right)\left(\frac{\rho g}{P_0}\right)$, incorporating Landau quantization, de Haas-van Alphen oscillations, and Projected Shell Model (PSM) weak-interaction transitions for the $^{29}\mathrm{Na}\text{--}^{29}\mathrm{Mg}$ Urca pair.
papers.reason: This paper investigates crustal nuclear Urca neutrino cooling under quantizing magnetic fields and thermal excitation, providing a novel physical mechanism to explain the anomalously high surface temperatures of magnetars.

papers.title: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
papers.result: Nuclear experimental variance reduction on macroscopic stellar properties is bounded by core equation-of-state (EOS) freedom via $\mathcal{T}_X \le 1 - \mathcal{B}_{{\rm core},X}/V_X$. For a reference $1.4M_\odot$ neutron star, tidal deformability $\Lambda = \frac{2}{3}k_2 C^{-5}$ with compactness $C = GM/(Rc^2)$ exhibits an extreme conditional cancellation between logarithmic radius $x = \ln(R/1\,\mathrm{km})$ and Love number $z = \ln k_2$ with anti-correlation $\rho = -0.952$, suppressing nuclear constraints on tides to $1.38\%$. Pairing a pulsar radius measurement of $\sigma_R = 0.3\,\mathrm{km}$ with binary tidal deformability $\widetilde{\Lambda} = \frac{16[(1+12q)\Lambda_1 + (q+12)q^4\Lambda_2]}{13(1+q)^5}$ measured to $\sigma_{\ln\widetilde{\Lambda}} = 0.1$ removes $44\text{--}68\%$ of the logarithmic Love-number variance $\ln k_2$.
papers.problem: High-density core equation-of-state uncertainties limit the direct translation of low-density nuclear precision into neutron-star macroscopic constraints, while core profile freedom permits neutron stars with nearly identical radii (differing by only $2.86\,\mathrm{m}$) to exhibit a $10.64\%$ discrepancy in tidal deformability.
papers.method: Formulated a variance decomposition framework partitioning total observable variance into core variance and nuclear parameter conditional variance $V_X = \mathcal{B}_{{\rm core},X} + \operatorname{Var}_{\theta|\mathcal{D}}\mu_X$. Integrated Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations and relativistic tidal perturbation equations across matching densities $n_m \in \{1.1, 1.25, 1.5\}n_0$ with piecewise constant sound speed cores $s_j = (dP/d\epsilon)_j$. Conditioned parameters using Bayesian likelihood updates combining GW170817 binary tides and NICER X-ray pulse profile modeling of PSR J0030+0451, PSR J0740+6620, and PSR J0437-4715.
papers.reason: The paper quantitatively derives theoretical bounds on how laboratory nuclear precision constrains neutron-star structure and demonstrates how multimessenger radius and tidal measurements resolve inner density profile degeneracies.

papers.title: Probing for relativistic outflows in the Ultraluminous X-ray pulsar RX J0209.6-7427
papers.result: The broadband continuum during the super-Eddington outburst ($L_{\mathrm{bol}} = (9.5 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{38}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$) is well described by two modified blackbodies ($k T_{\mathrm{mbb},1} = 0.259 \pm 0.005\ \mathrm{keV}$, $k T_{\mathrm{mbb},2} = 1.0 \pm 0.2\ \mathrm{keV}$) and a Comptonised component ($k T_{\mathrm{e}} = 3.6 \pm 0.1\ \mathrm{keV}$, optical depth $\tau = 9.98_{-0.38}^{+0.07}$). High-resolution emission lines reveal a multiphase, slowly moving ($v_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 10 \pm 200\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) photoionised/collisional plasma with electron density $n_{\mathrm{e}} \sim 3 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ derived from the $\mathrm{O\ VII}$ triplet ratio ($R = 0.40$). Absorption modelling provides evidence for a relativistically blueshifted ultrafast outflow with line-of-sight velocity $v_{\mathrm{LOS,xabs}} = -30000 \pm 300\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}} \approx -0.1c$.
papers.problem: Investigating whether super-critical accretion onto a strongly magnetised neutron star launches relativistic ultrafast outflows (UFOs) and constraining the physical properties and ionisation state of the circum-source emitting and absorbing plasma in pulsating ultraluminous X-ray sources (pULXs).
papers.method: Analysis of high-signal-to-noise *XMM-Newton* RGS and EPIC-pn spectra using SPEX (v3.07.03) with Cash statistics ($C$-stat). The analysis employs a multi-component continuum (`mbb + mbb + comt`), Gaussian blind line searches, and multi-dimensional grid fitting comparing collisional ionisation equilibrium (`cie`) and photoionised emission (`pion`) and absorption (`xabs`) plasma models.
papers.reason: This paper presents high-resolution XMM-Newton RGS spectroscopy of the Be-XRB pulsar RX J0209.6-7427 during its super-Eddington outburst, offering empirical constraints on dense circumstellar plasma and candidate ultrafast outflows in pulsating ULXs.

papers.result: The white dwarf spin, beat, and orbital periods are determined as $P_{\mathrm{spin}} = 4.2683^{+0.0001}_{-0.0002}\,\mathrm{h}$, $P_{\mathrm{beat}} = 48.75^{+0.07}_{-0.10}\,\mathrm{h}$, and $P_{\mathrm{orb}} = 4.6779^{+0.0010}_{-0.0007}\,\mathrm{h}$, yielding an asynchronous ratio $P_{\mathrm{spin}}/P_{\mathrm{orb}} = 0.9124 \pm 0.0002$ (degree of asynchronism $\approx 8.8\%$) at $L_X \sim 2.2 \times 10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$. The system is identified as a Class 2 (Case B) asynchronous polar with complete two-pole switching, where power at $\omega$ and $\omega_{\mathrm{beat}}$ is suppressed and shifted into $\Omega$, sideband $2\omega - \Omega$, and beat second harmonic $2\omega_{\mathrm{beat}} = 7.16 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{rad\ s^{-1}}$.

papers.method: Analysis of Chandra ACIS-S 0.1--7 keV light curves using Lomb-Scargle periodograms combined with a 20-parameter two-pole switching model $R(t) = \max[M_1(t)B_1(t)S_1(t), 0] + \max[M_2(t)B_2(t)S_2(t), 0] + E$ and beat relation $1/P_{\mathrm{beat}} = 1/P_{\mathrm{spin}} - 1/P_{\mathrm{orb}}$ (assuming $P_{\mathrm{spin}} < P_{\mathrm{orb}}$), sampled via `emcee` MCMC with Poisson log-likelihood $\ell(\theta) = \sum_{i=1}^n [y_i \ln(f(t_i, \theta) E_i) - f(t_i, \theta) E_i]$ and verified by independent $O-C$ pulse timing of 21 X-ray pulses.

papers.reason: AT 2024qfm is the most X-ray luminous LFBOT observed at early times ($L_{\rm x} \approx 10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$), providing critical observational constraints on central engine driving, high-energy reprocessing efficiency, and relativistic shock-CSM interaction.

papers.title: The XRISM view of the front and rear ejecta dynamics in Tycho's SNR
papers.result: Resolve unambiguously resolves Doppler splitting of K-shell lines into front (blueshifted) and rear (redshifted) shells. The line-of-sight velocities are $v_{\mathrm{front}}(\mathrm{Si}) = -3320 \pm 60\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ and $v_{\mathrm{back}}(\mathrm{Si}) = +3920 \pm 100\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ ($v_{\mathrm{front}}(\mathrm{S}) = -3250 \pm 50\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $v_{\mathrm{back}}(\mathrm{S}) = +3830 \pm 80\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), showing a rear shell expansion $\sim 600\text{--}700\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ faster than the front side (asymmetry $\sim 16\%$). Fe exhibits lower velocities ($v_{\mathrm{front}}(\mathrm{Fe}) = -2510\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $v_{\mathrm{back}}(\mathrm{Fe}) = +3330\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) with velocity ratio $v_{\mathrm{Fe}}/v_{\mathrm{Si}} \approx 0.75$, consistent with projected radius ratio $R_{\mathrm{Fe}}/R_{\mathrm{Si}} \approx 0.85$. The front-side flux fraction $R = \frac{I_{\mathrm{front}}}{I_{\mathrm{front}} + I_{\mathrm{back}}}$ reaches $57\% \pm 1\%$ globally for Si and up to $70\%\text{--}80\%$ in the northeast.
papers.problem: Previous CCD-based observations suffered from limited spectral resolution ($\nobreak >100\ \mathrm{eV}$), measuring only flux-weighted line-of-sight mean velocities that conflated intrinsic kinematic asymmetry with shell surface brightness asymmetry.
papers.method: XRISM/Resolve $1.75\text{--}7.0\ \mathrm{keV}$ spectra across 5 pointings (149 pixels) were analyzed with Bayesian nested sampling (BXA/Sherpa/Xspec) using multi-Gaussian models over a synchrotron power law ($\Gamma \approx 2.75\text{--}2.83$). Line complexes of Si, S, Ar, Ca, and Fe were modeled with shared Doppler shifts per shell and global broadening ($\sigma \approx 16.5\text{--}23.7\ \mathrm{eV}$ at $2\ \mathrm{keV}$, corresponding to velocity dispersion $\Delta V_z \approx 2475\text{--}3555\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), and synthesized into 3D velocity maps with Chandra proper motions ($V_{xy}$) assuming distance $d = 3.5\ \mathrm{kpc}$ via $V_{z,\mathrm{mean}} = V_{z,\mathrm{front}} \times \frac{I_{\mathrm{front}}}{I_{\mathrm{front}}+I_{\mathrm{back}}} + V_{z,\mathrm{back}} \times \left(1 - \frac{I_{\mathrm{front}}}{I_{\mathrm{front}}+I_{\mathrm{back}}}\right)$.
papers.reason: This work presents the first high-resolution X-ray calorimetric 3D mapping of ejecta dynamics in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve, resolving Doppler splitting to disentangle velocity asymmetry from flux asymmetry.

papers.title: Radiation-Hydrodynamical Modeling of Accretion Columns in Ultraluminous X-ray Pulsars
papers.result: Across disparate surface magnetic fields ($B_* \sim 6\times 10^{12}\text{--}1.6\times 10^{13}\,{\rm G}$) and accretion luminosities ($L_{\rm X} \sim 2.0\times 10^{39}\text{--}4.7\times 10^{39}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$), all modeled ULXPs develop an extended radiation-dominated sinking region with the radiation sonic surface ($a_{\rm rad} = |v|$) clustered tightly at $r_{\rm sonic} \simeq 15.032\,{\rm km}$ (NGC 300 ULX-1), $15.079\,{\rm km}$ (Swift J0243.6$+$6124), and $15.004\,{\rm km}$ (SMC X-3). Thermal mound heights defined by $\tau_\parallel^{\rm ff} = 1$ scale strongly with parameters, reaching $h_{\rm th} = 1.534\,{\rm km}$, $0.532\,{\rm km}$, and $0.070\,{\rm km}$ respectively, with residual flow velocities approaching the stellar surface at $|v| \sim 0.01c$.
papers.problem: Previous models of super-Eddington accretion columns relied on prescribed kinematic velocity profiles or decoupled two-fluid temperatures, failing to self-consistently solve the coupled dynamics, sonic surface locations, and thermal mound depths in ULXPs.
papers.method: Solves steady-state, one-dimensional cross-section averaged two-fluid radiation-hydrodynamical (RHD) equations along magnetic dipole field lines for 1D electrons ($\gamma_e = 3$, $U_e = \frac{1}{2}n_e k_B T_e$) and 3D ions ($\gamma_i = 5/3$, $U_i = \frac{3}{2}n_i k_B T_i$). The system couples radiation sound speed gradients $\frac{{\rm d}a_{\rm rad}}{{\rm d}r} = \frac{a_{\rm rad}}{2v}\frac{{\rm d}v}{{\rm d}r} + \frac{3a_{\rm rad}}{2r} - \frac{\sigma_{\parallel}\gamma_{\rm rad}\dot{M}}{2m_{p}c\,a_{\rm rad}A(r)}\mathcal{E}(r)$ with cyclotron emission $\dot{U}_{\rm cyc}^{\rm emit}$ and electron-ion Coulomb transfer, closed by free-streaming upper boundary conditions $F_{\rm rad}(r_{\rm top}) = (c + \frac{4}{3}v_{\rm top})U_{\rm rad}(r_{\rm top})$ and a stellar surface mirror boundary $F_{\rm rad}(R_*) = 0$ with numerical stagnation $|v(R_*)| \lesssim 0.02c$.
papers.reason: This paper presents a self-consistent two-fluid radiation-hydrodynamical framework for super-Eddington accretion columns in ultraluminous X-ray pulsars (ULXPs), directly addressing the physical mechanisms of high-energy compact object emission and deceleration dynamics.

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.result: The binary reaches a Dual Horizon-MAD (DH-MAD) state where the dimensionless horizon flux saturates at $\phi_{\rm BH} \sim 20$ after $\sim 23$ orbits, launching relativistic jets with average Poynting luminosity $L_{\rm Poyn}/\dot{M} = 0.01$ (efficiency $\eta = 1\%$). Individual BH accretion rates show dominant periodicity at $f \sim 0.9f_{\rm orb}$ (with secondary peaks at $f \sim 1.8f_{\rm orb}$), while total accretion modulates at $f \sim 1.8f_{\rm orb}$ and dimensionless horizon magnetic flux oscillates at $f \sim 0.4f_{\rm orb}$.
papers.problem: Investigating long-term circumbinary disk accretion and magnetic flux accumulation in equal-mass binary black holes in full general relativity to determine cavity magnetic structure, minidisk survival, and multi-messenger electromagnetic signatures.
papers.method: 3D full GRMHD simulations using the Einstein Toolkit with LeanBSSN for dynamical spacetime and IllinoisGRMHD for magnetohydrodynamics, modeling an equal-mass ($q=1$), non-spinning ($\chi_1=\chi_2=0$) binary at initial separation $d/M=30$ with circumbinary poloidal magnetic field ($\beta_{\rm ini}=52.42$) evolved past $t \simeq 52,000\,GM/c^3$.
papers.reason: This work presents long-term full GRMHD simulations of circumbinary disk accretion onto a supermassive binary black hole, discovering a Dual Horizon-MAD regime with periodic accretion and jet emissions directly relevant to compact object high-energy observations.

papers.title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
papers.result: In underdense void environments (Case A), relativistic jets with injection Lorentz factor $\Gamma = 12$ accelerate to $\Gamma > 20$ via recollimation shocks, maintaining an average propagation speed $v_{\rm head} \sim 0.72c$ and reaching a total scale of $\sim 9\ \mathrm{Mpc}$ in $t \approx 19.6\ \mathrm{Myr}$ with an aspect ratio of $\sim 20$ and energy $E_{\rm inj} \approx 0.9 \times 10^{62}\ \mathrm{erg}$. In cluster media (Cases B and C), jets stall at $\sim 1.5\text{--}2\ \mathrm{Mpc}$ ($E_{\rm inj} \sim [1.2, 3.4] \times 10^{62}\ \mathrm{erg}$ at $[26.1, 76.6]\ \mathrm{Myr}$). High relativistic thrust at $\Gamma \ge 12$ strongly suppresses Kelvin-Helmholtz and kink instabilities (FFT fluctuation power $\sum |F(k)|^2 / N \lesssim 10^{-2}$ at $\lesssim 3\ \mathrm{Mpc}$), preventing lateral disruption until the jet head.
papers.problem: Understanding the physical survival mechanisms and observational scarcity of multi-Mpc giant radio galaxies (GRGs, such as Porphyrion spanning $\sim 7\ \mathrm{Mpc}$), particularly whether their terminal reach is constrained by destructive MHD instabilities, ambient density gradients, or central engine lifetimes.
papers.method: 3D relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) simulations using the GPU-accelerated code `gPLUTO` with the Taub–Matthews equation of state. Jets are injected with power $P_{\rm jet} = 3.5 \times 10^{46}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, bulk Lorentz factor $\Gamma = 12$, density $\rho_j = 5 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{amu\ cm^{-3}}$, magnetization $\sigma = B_j^2 / (4\pi \Gamma^2 \rho_j h_j) = 0.1$, and nozzle radius $r_j = 2\ \mathrm{kpc}$. Synchrotron emissivity $\mathcal{I}'_{\rm syn}$ at $144\ \mathrm{MHz}$ is modeled assuming non-thermal electron energy density fraction $\epsilon = 0.5$, power-law index $p = 2.2$ over $10^2 \le \gamma \le 10^6$, and Doppler beaming factor $\mathcal{D}$. Ambient gas is set via a King $\beta$-profile ($\rho_c = 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{amu\ cm^{-3}}$, $r_c = 33\ \mathrm{kpc}$, $\beta = 0.55$, $kT \sim 1.1\ \mathrm{keV}$).
papers.reason: The paper investigates the propagation dynamics, recollimation shocks, and lateral stability of extraordinary relativistic jets on multi-Mpc scales using 3D RMHD simulations, directly relevant to relativistic jets and compact object outflows.

papers.title: Evaluating VLT SPHERE for Probing Diffuse Circumstellar Regions of Evolved Stars
papers.result: No extended circumstellar emission or near-infrared excess is detected across the 7 targets; injection-recovery tests establish contrast sensitivity limits of $\Delta m \sim 3.5\,\mathrm{mag}$ in J1 ($1.19\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) and $\Delta m \sim 2.0\,\mathrm{mag}$ in K1 ($2.10\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) relative to the residual coronagraphic PSF halo.
papers.problem: Direct sub-arcsecond imaging constraints on the morphology and mass-loss mechanisms of diffuse circumstellar material around evolved massive stars (RSGs and YSGs) are lacking, and symmetric diffuse structures suffer from self-subtraction in standard ADI.
papers.method: Reference-star differential imaging (RDI) with SPHERE/IRDIS pupil-tracking coronagraphy, combined with Radon-transform PCA projection modeling to reconstruct and subtract the instrument halo, and HDUST 3D radiative-transfer modeling.
papers.reason: This work evaluates the detection limits of VLT/SPHERE high-contrast imaging for diffuse circumstellar material around evolved massive stars, providing direct observational constraints on pre-supernova mass loss and CSM environments.

papers.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
papers.result: Electron phase-space holes (EHs) generate localized perpendicular currents via $\vec{E}_{\perp}\times\vec{B}_0$ drift that directly drive electrostatic Bernstein harmonics and electromagnetic electron cyclotron harmonics in weakly magnetized plasmas ($\omega_{ce}/\omega_{pe}=0.54$), while electromagnetic O- and X-mode waves are directly excited by $\phi$-well currents; under strong magnetization ($\omega_{ce}/\omega_{pe}=5.4$), perpendicular currents are suppressed and surfatron acceleration across $\phi$ wells accelerates electrons to $|U_x|>U_{de,0}=0.47c$.
papers.problem: Investigating how electron bi-stream instabilities and the formation of electron phase-space holes (EHs) in magnetized plasmas excite coherent electromagnetic radiation and govern non-thermal particle acceleration across different magnetization regimes.
papers.method: 2.5D fully kinetic relativistic electromagnetic PIC simulations with ACRONYM using mass ratio $m_p/m_e=1836$, grid size $N_x\times N_y=2048\times 2048$, resolution $\Delta x=\Delta y\approx 1.24\lambda_{De}$, and current-to-wave energy transfer diagnosed via $P=-\mathrm{Re}[\tilde{\vec{J}}^{*}\cdot\tilde{\vec{E}}]$ in $(\vec{k},\omega)$ space.
papers.reason: This PIC study provides a direct current-driven mechanism for coherent electromagnetic radiation from electron phase-space holes without requiring non-linear wave conversion or population inversion, offering valuable kinetic insight for coherent radio transients like solar zebra patterns and fast radio bursts.

papers.title: On extracting Science information from a large data set of RXTE X-ray binary spectra using KDE technique
papers.result: High-probability ($p > 0.99$) black hole systems occupy soft-state spectral regimes characterized by low blackbody temperature $kT_b < 1.05\,\mathrm{keV}$ (rank $< 0.25$) and high blackbody flux ratio $f_{\rm ratio} > 0.6$ (rank $> 0.88$), whereas neutron star systems exhibit harder emission with $kT_b > 1.6\,\mathrm{keV}$, photon index $\Gamma > 3$, $f_{\rm ratio} > 0.3$, and reduced $\chi^2 > 1.6$. Furthermore, the uniqueness metric successfully isolated the rare reflection-dominated state of neutron star EXO 1745-248 modeled by gravitational reflection (`relxillCp`).
papers.problem: Addressing the interpretability and black-box limitations of machine learning classifiers in X-ray astronomy while determining the physical spectral criteria that distinguish black hole from neutron star compact objects in low-mass X-ray binaries.
papers.method: The Direct Incidence Method (DIM) discretizes $N_{\rm var}$ rank-ordered spectral variables into integer vectors $\vec{IV} \in \{0, \dots, N_{\rm bin}-1\}^{N_{\rm var}}$, evaluating class likelihood via KDE with a power-law kernel: $P_c(\vec{IV}) = \frac{1}{N_c} \sum_{\vec{IV'}} \frac{I_c(\vec{IV'})}{(D+s)^p}$, where $D = \sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^{N_{\rm var}} (IV'_j - IV_j)^2}$, $p=4$, and $s=0.5$. Outlier and unique spectra are identified via uniqueness metric $U(\vec{IV}) = \sum_{j=0}^{c_{\rm max}} \frac{1}{N_c} \sum_{\vec{IV'}} I_c(\vec{IV'}) D^{pd}$.
papers.reason: The paper develops an interpretable Kernel Density Estimation and Direct Incidence Method applied to 14,855 RXTE LMXB spectra, establishing quantitative parameter boundaries that distinguish black hole from neutron star systems and identifying rare reflection-dominated states.

papers.title: Survey of Compact Sources for Pulsars and Exotic Objects-II. Precision Timing of Millisecond Pulsar J1840+1102
papers.result:
Obtained a 2.7-year phase-connected timing solution for PSR J1840+1102 with post-fit RMS residual of $\approx 2.14\,\mu\mathrm{s}$, spin frequency $
u \approx 624.79\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $\dot{
u} \approx -4.56 	imes 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{Hz\,s^{-1}}$, $P = 1.60\,\mathrm{ms}$, $P_B \approx 1.68\,\mathrm{d}$, $e \approx 1.84 	imes 10^{-6}$, and $\mathrm{DM} = 98.8\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$. papers.problem: Constructing a coherent phase-connected timing model, characterizing binary orbital properties, identifying high-energy counterparts, and measuring interstellar propagation effects for the newly discovered eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102.
papers.method: Utilized uGMRT Band-4 ($550\text{--}750\,\mathrm{MHz}$) and Band-3 ($300\text{--}500\,\mathrm{MHz}$) coherent dedispersion timing observations reduced via PRESTO and TEMPO2. papers.reason: This paper presents precision timing, DM analysis, gamma-ray pulsation detection, and ISM scattering measurements for the eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102, providing empirical constraints on compact object high-energy emission and turbulent plasma propagation effects.

papers.title: Finite-temperature quark dynamics in proto-neutron stars: Maximum baryonic mass and radial oscillations
papers.result: Deconfinement quark degrees of freedom soften the EOS, reducing maximum gravitational mass from $M_G \approx 2.41\,M_\odot$ in pure hadronic matter to $M_G \sim 2.1\,M_\odot$ in hybrid stars. Crucially, quark softening reverses the evolutionary ordering of the maximum baryonic mass from increasing during cooling ($C_{\mathrm{S1}} < C_{\mathrm{S2}} < C_{\mathrm{Cold}}$ in RMF) to progressively decreasing ($C_{\mathrm{Cold}} < C_{\mathrm{S2}} < C_{\mathrm{S1}}$ in PNJL and EPNJL), opening a delayed-collapse window of width $\sim 0.1\,M_\odot$ for hot PNSs with $M_B > 2.42\,M_\odot$. In the hot neutrino-free stage S2, fundamental radial oscillation frequencies obey $f_0^{\text{RMF-only}} > f_0^{\text{EPNJL}} > f_0^{\text{PNJL}}$, with EPNJL and PNJL dropping by $\approx 16.3\%$ and $\approx 36.0\%$ at $M_B = 2.500\,M_\odot$ while remaining dynamically stable ($\omega_0^2 > 0$).
papers.problem: How finite-temperature quark dynamics and deconfinement phase transitions during neutrino trapping ($S=1, Y_{L_e}=0.4$), deleptonization ($S=2, \mu_{L_e}=0$), and cooling impact the maximum baryonic mass thresholds and dynamical radial stability of proto-neutron stars.
papers.method: Hadronic matter is modeled via relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory with $\sigma, \omega^\mu, \rho_3^\mu$ meson fields ($M^* = m_N - g_\sigma \phi_\sigma$); quark matter is modeled using three-flavor PNJL and EPNJL models with Polyakov loops $\Phi, \bar{\Phi}$ and entanglement coupling $G(\Phi,\bar{\Phi}) = G_S [1 - \alpha_1 \Phi\bar{\Phi} - \alpha_2(\Phi^3+\bar{\Phi}^3)]$. Phase coexistence is constructed via Gibbs equilibrium ($P_H = P_Q$, matching chemical potentials and temperature), coupled to the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and linear radial pulsation eigenvalue equations to evaluate $\omega_0^2$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates how finite-temperature quark dynamics alter proto-neutron star (PNS) evolution, identifying a reversal of maximum baryonic mass ordering that governs delayed collapse to black holes in core-collapse supernova central engines.

papers.title: Reliability of Fermi/GBM spectral-catalogue parameters for gamma-ray burst population studies
papers.result: The core Comptonized (COMP) spectral shape is highly stable across the catalogue transition at GRB180712358, with effect sizes $|r_{\rm rb}| < 0.10$ across all ten physical parameters for the nominal $1024\text{ ms}$ long GRBs. Brighter bursts yield smaller formal parameter errors ($\gamma_{\rm br} = -0.667$ to $-0.750$) but systematically higher reported fit statistics ($b_{\rm br} = 0.169\text{--}0.439$) and stronger COMP-to-BAND improvements $\Delta S_{\rm CB} = S_{\rm COMP} - S_{\rm BAND} > 11.83$. BAND low-energy parameters $\alpha$ and $E_{\rm peak}$ remain reliable when error-bounded ($37.6\%\text{--}94.6\%$ usable), whereas the high-energy index $\beta$ is poorly constrained across the full catalogue (usable in only $1.9\%\text{--}37.5\%$ of bursts).
papers.problem: Apparent multi-component GRB population clusters and temporal evolutions in the Fermi/GBM catalogue are frequently contaminated by instrumental selection effects, differing peak-flux integration timescales ($64\text{ ms}$ vs. $1024\text{ ms}$), and a discrete software/statistic transition at GRB180712358 (Castor C-STAT in period B vs. PSTAT in period A).
papers.method: Statistical meta-analysis of $3337$ Fermi/GBM GRBs comparing empirical models (PLAW, COMP, BAND, SBPL) across catalogue periods A and B using standardized rank regression $Z_R(r_{\rm stat}) = b_{\rm br}Z_R(\log_{10}F) + b_\nu Z_R(\nu) + \epsilon$, bootstrap effect-size rank-biserial correlations $r_{\rm rb}$, and model selection thresholds $\Delta S_{\rm PC} = S_{\rm PLAW} - S_{\rm COMP} > 8.58$ and $\Delta S_{\rm CB} = S_{\rm COMP} - S_{\rm BAND} > 11.83$ based on Poisson deviance $C = 2\sum_i [\mu_i - n_i + n_i \ln(n_i / \mu_i)]$.
papers.reason: This work establishes critical methodological constraints on Fermi/GBM GRB spectral catalogue parameters, preventing relativistic jet and compact object population studies from confusing catalogue processing transitions and brightness-dependent fit statistics with intrinsic astrophysical evolution.

papers.title: Interpreting the $γ$-Ray Emission of the Cygnus X region with a Combined Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3 Scenario
papers.result: Cygnus OB2 wind termination shock (WTS) alone cannot reproduce the PeV $\gamma$-ray emission due to severe particle escape under Kolmogorov/Kraichnan diffusion or spectral discrepancy under Bohm diffusion ($\\eta = 0$ or $\\eta = 0.11$). Instead, the microquasar Cygnus X-3 with a proton cutoff energy $E_c = 50\,\mathrm{PeV}$ and an escape fraction $\eta_{\rm esc} = 0.005\text{--}0.009$ into the ambient ISM ($D(E) = 4.0 \times 10^{26}(E/1\,\mathrm{GeV})^{1/3}\,\mathrm{cm^2\,s^{-1}}$) reproduces the observed PeV photons and extended $\gamma$-ray halo.
papers.problem: LHAASO observed extended $\gamma$-ray emission reaching PeV energies with a $1/r$ profile in Cygnus X alongside IceCube neutrino excess, posing the question of whether the PeVatron origin is driven by the massive cluster Cygnus OB2 or the microquasar Cygnus X-3.
papers.method: The authors solve the spherically symmetric steady-state proton transport equation $\frac{\partial N}{\partial t} = \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial}{\partial r}[r^2 D(E)\frac{\partial N}{\partial r}] - \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial}{\partial r}[r^2 \tilde{u}(r)N] + \frac{\partial}{\partial E}[\dot{E}N] + Q$ discretized on a $1000\times 1000$ $(r, E)$ grid, incorporating adiabatic expansion and $pp$ energy losses $\dot{E}_{\rm pp} = K_{\rm pp}(1 + 0.055L + 0.0073L^2)n_g E$, coupled with GAMERA radiation calculations.
papers.reason: The paper investigates the PeVatron nature and multi-messenger emission of the Cygnus X region by evaluating a combined hadronic model of the microquasar Cygnus X-3, Cygnus OB2, and Galactic cosmic rays, directly relevant to relativistic jet and compact object high-energy astrophysics.

papers.title: Luminosity function of millisecond pulsars in globular clusters from their gamma-ray emission
papers.result: Using a baseline sample of 36 globular clusters, the universal log-normal MSP gamma-ray luminosity function yields median parameters and 68% credible intervals of $\log_{10}(L_{0}/\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}) = 33.4^{+0.4}_{-0.2}$ and $\sigma_{L} = 1.3^{+0.4}_{-0.5}$ (with mean luminosity $\langle L_{\gamma}\rangle = L_{0}\exp(\sigma_{L}^{2}/2)$). Inferred cluster gamma-ray MSP counts are $\log_{10}N_{\rm Ter5} = 1.8^{+0.2}_{-0.2}$ ($N_{\rm Ter5}\sim 70_{-24}^{+42}$), $\log_{10}N_{\rm 47\,Tuc} = 1.1^{+0.3}_{-0.2}$ ($N_{\rm 47\,Tuc}\sim 13$), and $\log_{10}N_{\rm NGC\,1851} = 0.7^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ ($N_{\rm NGC\,1851}\sim 5$). Analyzing full SEDs rules out $\sigma_{L} < 0.5$ at $>3\sigma$ and prevents the overestimation of dispersion found when using integrated energy fluxes ($\sigma_{L} = 1.5^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$).
papers.problem: Inferring the intrinsic gamma-ray luminosity function of MSPs in globular clusters previously relied on integrated gamma-ray fluxes paired with empirical multi-wavelength proxies (e.g., stellar encounter rates) to fix source counts, introducing strong model bias and parameter degeneracies. Furthermore, scaling conventional likelihood nested sampling to multiple clusters suffers from an intractable high-dimensional latent space.
papers.method: The authors construct a forward simulator where MSP luminosities in each globular cluster are sampled from a universal log-normal luminosity function $\frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}L_{\gamma}}=\frac{1}{L_{\gamma}\sigma_{L}\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\left(-\frac{(\ln{L_{\gamma}}-\ln{L_{0}})^{2}}{2\sigma_{L}^{2}}\right)$ with individual spectra modeled by PLEC4, yielding individual flux $F_{{\rm MSP},c} = \frac{L_{c}}{4\pi d_{I}^{2}}$. They implement Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) using Neural Ratio Estimation (NRE, `swyft`) to perform amortized Bayesian inference directly on 0.1–100 GeV Fermi-LAT SEDs and phase-resolved ON/OFF spectra, marginalizing over unconstrained cluster MSP populations $N_{I}$ under log-uniform priors.
papers.reason: This paper presents a simulation-based Bayesian inference framework to constrain the universal gamma-ray luminosity function of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in globular clusters directly from Fermi-LAT SEDs, providing important population constraints and methodology for high-energy compact object studies.

papers.title: Tidal effects of bulk viscosity in neutron stars
papers.result: Bulk viscosity exhibits a resonant peak $\zeta_{\max} = \frac{n_b C^2}{4B}\frac{1}{\omega}$ at $\omega = \gamma$. While the effective tidal deformability $\Xi^{(\mathrm{eff})}$ monotonically decreases with compactness $C$, the global dissipative tidal deformability $\Xi(C)$ peaks at intermediate compactness due to the competition between $\Xi \propto C^{-6}$ and the expanding direct Urca core volume fraction $(R_{\mathrm{dU}}/R_*)^3$. Causality imposes strict upper limits $\tau_{d,A}^{\mathrm{causal}} = \frac{G m_A}{c^3 C_A^2} p_{2,A}$ and $\Xi_A \le \Xi_{\mathrm{causal}} = \frac{p_{2,A}}{C_A^2} \Lambda_A$, which limits the maximum mass configuration to $\Xi^{\mathrm{TOV}} \simeq 0.5244\left(\frac{\tau_d}{\mu\mathrm{s}}\right)$.
papers.problem: How bulk viscosity driven by weak direct Urca processes in $npe$ matter determines out-of-equilibrium dissipative tidal deformability and lag time during binary neutron star inspiral, and whether these dissipative tidal effects can be constrained by causality or probed by gravitational-wave detectors.
papers.method: The authors construct four cold $npe$ equations of state (MDI-1–4) using the momentum-dependent interaction model under beta equilibrium and charge neutrality. In the subthermal linear regime, direct Urca bulk viscosity $\zeta(\gamma) = \frac{n_b C^2}{2B}\frac{\gamma}{\omega^2+\gamma^2}$ is evaluated for oscillation frequencies $\omega = 10^3, 10^4~\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and mapped to the macroscopic tidal lag time $\tau_{d,A} = \frac{p_{2,A}\nu_A}{c^2 C_A}$ and dimensionless dissipative tidal deformability $\Xi$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates bulk viscosity driven by direct Urca processes in $npe$ neutron star matter and quantitatively models the dissipative tidal deformability $\Xi$ and tidal lag time $\tau_d$ during binary neutron star inspiral, providing theoretical and causality constraints for gravitational-wave detections.

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.result: The leading dissipative tidal response is governed by shear viscosity (with bulk viscosity suppressed in equilibrium tides due to $\Theta = 0$). For realistic equations of state (APR, SLy4, BSk24, DD2) at $1.4 M_\odot$ and redshifted temperature $T_\infty = 10^5\,\mathrm{K}$, the dimensionless dissipative Love number is $k_2^{(1)} \sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$. Dissipative absorption enters the gravitational wave energy flux at relative 4PN order via $\mathcal{F}_{\rm tot} = \mathcal{F}_N (1 + \mathcal{A}_{\rm diss} v^8)$ with $\mathcal{A}_{\rm diss} = \frac{15}{16}\sum_{a=1}^2 (m_a/M)^4 C_a^{-6} k_{2,a}^{(1)} \sim 0.08\text{--}0.18$, accelerating the inspiral and producing a cumulative dephasing of $\delta\mathcal{N}_{\rm GW} = -\frac{5GM\mathcal{A}_{\rm diss}}{96\nu c^3}(f_f - f_i) \sim -10^{-3}\text{ to }-10^{-2}$ cycles over $20\text{--}1000\,\mathrm{Hz}$.
